name: Lambchop
label: Merge
lede: Kurt Wagner kept laying hardwood floors in Nashville while his oversized band picked up a name from a lawyer's letter and its first big audience in Europe.

eras.title: Wood floors, a bedroom, a record shop
eras.text: Three high school friends in Nashville made tapes in a bedroom and played wherever they could, especially the record shop run by Kurt Wagner's wife. The trio kept growing into a loose, oversized ensemble.

years.h: Three Nashville friends record Posterchild tapes in a bedroom
years.p: [[Kurt Wagner|1fb3ef7d-c947-4f7e-8627-69e93ef4bdd0]], bassist [[Marc Trovillion|4647a834-8c3e-4cbd-81cf-31ba1bb61353]] and guitarist Jim Watkins form a trio called Posterchild. They record in Trovillion's bedroom and self-release cassettes.
years.xp:
Wagner was born October 5, 1959, to Northern parents who moved to Nashville when he was two. He went to art school in Memphis, then worked as a carpenter laying wood floors.

He kept laying floors before and after Lambchop's 1990s success.

years.h: Lucy's Record Shop becomes the band's home stage
years.p: The shop was founded by Wagner's wife, Mary Mancini. The band that plays there regularly is now seven people, including Jonathan Marx and drummer Steve Goodhue.

years.h: A split single with Crop Circle Hoax reaches lawyer George Regis
years.p: Posterchild's 7-inch An Open Fresca + A Moist Towelette catches the ear of entertainment lawyer George Regis, who soon acts for a band with a nearly identical name.

eras.title: A lawyer's letter, a label in Chapel Hill
eras.text: A legal letter forced a new name, and Merge gave the renamed band a home. Pedal steel, sax and organ came in, and by Thriller Lambchop were chasing Muscle Shoals soul as much as Nashville country.

years.h: Poster Children's lawyer sends a cease-and-desist
years.p: The Illinois band [[Poster Children|050f867a-ed04-4a38-9f6e-b9bf84ca664b]] objects to the name Posterchild. Wagner's group rejects REN and Pinnacles of Cream before settling on Lambchop.
years.xp:
The entertainment lawyer George Regis acted for Poster Children. Wagner's band, by now bigger than a trio, tried several names before Lambchop stuck.

The renamed lineup added singer and saxophonist [[Deanna Varagona|d8e78a9c-0001-49aa-bbd1-c6a9031b9268]], pedal steel player [[Paul Niehaus|f84893b8-2c33-4218-adc4-4169954610d8]] and organist John Delworth.

years.h: Merge puts out the single Nine
years.p: Lambchop sign to Merge, the Chapel Hill label run by [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]]'s [[Mac McCaughan|8841967d-3914-4ab9-aca6-94781aa35288]] and [[Laura Ballance|1d11820c-e2a0-4ad7-8415-3d93c317c8cf]]. Their first release for it is the single Nine.

years.h: I Hope You're Sitting Down is also Jack's Tulips
years.p: The debut album on Merge carries two titles, one on each side of the sleeve.

years.h: How I Quit Smoking reaches for 1960s Nashville strings
years.p: Lush arrangements in the style of Nashville-sound records. Merge releases it in the US and City Slang in Europe.

years.h: Paul Burch joins on drums for the Hank EP
years.p: The Hank EP is the first appearance of drummer [[Paul Burch|e55af1dd-fc5e-4651-8508-42686e983a02]] with the band.

years.h: Thriller borrows three songs from East River Pipe
years.p: Wagner covers three songs by F.M. Cornog of [[East River Pipe|0e56780b-b99c-4078-a098-bba329db985d]] and leans into Southern soul. AllMusic calls the record sprawling and difficult.

eras.title: Ignored at home, booked in Europe's big rooms
eras.text: Kurt Wagner found a falsetto and Curtis Mayfield, backed his friend Vic Chesnutt, and made Nixon. Lambchop were suddenly playing concert halls in Europe.

years.h: Wagner's falsetto meets the songs of Curtis Mayfield
years.p: What Another Man Spills covers Curtis Mayfield and Frederick Knight. AllMusic compares the falsetto Wagner jumps to with [[Prince|070d193a-845c-479f-980e-bef15710653e]].

years.cap: Vic Chesnutt, The Salesman and Bernadette (1998).
years.h: The whole band backs [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]] on The Salesman and Bernadette
years.p: The Athens, Georgia songwriter Vic Chesnutt makes his 1998 album with the full Lambchop ensemble behind him.

years.h: Josh Rouse and Wagner share a record, Chester
years.p: Wagner teams up with Nashville singer-songwriter [[Josh Rouse|023d64c9-93db-4a20-8c5c-2efa1a53481a]] on a collaborative album.

years.h: Nixon ships with a reading list
years.p: A soul-steeped record about American history, with a bibliography in the liner notes. It's Lambchop's breakthrough, mostly in Europe.

years.h: Barely known in the US, Lambchop play London's Royal Festival Hall
years.p: The London show is recorded and sold as the tour-only release Queens Royal Trimma in 2000. Treasure Chest of the Enemy follows in 2001.
years.xp: Both were limited European tour EPs, released while Lambchop played bigger rooms abroad than at home.

years.h: Tools in the Dryer collects the odds and ends
years.p: Singles, compilation tracks and remixes get one home.

years.h: Is a Woman drops the horns and keeps the piano
years.p: After Nixon's horns and strings, a deliberately sparse, quiet album built around Wagner's voice and piano.

eras.title: Two albums at once
eras.text: Lambchop went maximal again with a pair of records, then kept shifting shape with electronic collaborators and Nashville players like William Tyler and Tony Crow. The era closed with the death of Vic Chesnutt.

years.cap: Kurt Wagner and bandmates live, August 8, 2004.
years.h: Lambchop release Aw Cmon and No You Cmon as a pair
years.p: Both albums are string-heavy, and both come out in February 2004.

years.h: Hands Off Cuba turn Lambchop electronic on the CoLAB EP
years.p: The experimental EP with the Nashville electronic duo is an early sign of where Wagner was headed.

years.h: The Woodwind Years adds a new Gettysburg Address
years.p: The full title is The Decline of Country & Western Civilization, Pt. 2: The Woodwind Years. It mixes unreleased tracks with a new piece, Gettysburg Address.

years.h: Damaged puts William Tyler and Tony Crow in the core
years.p: Fourteen songs. Mojo calls it an album of colossal strength and maturity.
years.xp:
Guitarist [[William Tyler|37e374de-ed4a-4bab-97ac-b6520971b0ed]] and pianist Tony Crow anchor a crowded credit list that also includes Paul Niehaus on steel guitar, Deanna Varagona on baritone sax, trombones, cellos, violins and a viola.

Reviews were generally good: Metacritic averages 81 out of 100, Pitchfork gives it 6.8 and PopMatters 9.

yt: Kurt Wagner, NPR Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: Ten albums in, Lambchop slow down for OH (Ohio)
years.p: AllMusic calls Lambchop's tenth album graceful and unhurried.

years.h: Vic Chesnutt dies on Christmas Day
years.p: [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], whose 1998 album Lambchop backed, dies after an overdose of muscle relaxants. Wagner dedicates the next Lambchop album to him.

eras.title: A record for Vic, then the machines
eras.text: Mr. M was a long goodbye to Vic Chesnutt. Then Lambchop lost a founder, and Kurt Wagner went off to make electronic music under another name and brought it back into the band.

years.h: Mr. M belongs to Vic Chesnutt
years.p: Eleven string-laden songs about love and loss, with the whole album dedicated to Chesnutt's memory.

years.h: Founding bassist Marc Trovillion dies at 56
years.p: Trovillion, who started Posterchild with Wagner in 1986 and recorded its first tapes in his bedroom, dies of a heart attack in October.

years.big: "...marry a musician about 15-20 years before you declare your candidacy."
years.h: Mary Mancini becomes Tennessee Democratic Party chair
years.p: Wagner's wife Mary Mancini, who founded Lucy's Record Shop, jokes about the fundraising advantage of her husband's job.
years.xp: Mancini was elected chair on January 10, 2015, the second woman to hold the post. She had run in the 2014 Democratic primary for State Senate District 21 and lost.

years.h: Wagner goes electronic as HeCTA
years.p: He launches the project on Merge with the album The Diet. Its sound feeds straight into the next Lambchop record.

years.cap: Lambchop at Castello Carrarese, Padova, Italy.
years.h: FLOTUS stands for For Love Often Turns Us Still
years.p: Wagner's voice, processed, floats over beats and orchestral arrangements. It's Lambchop's electronic turn.
years.xp: In 2017 Lambchop released The Hustle Unlimited, an orchestral rework of a FLOTUS track.

eras.title: Pen pals in lockdown
eras.text: Auto-Tune, a covers album, a pandemic and a paint factory in Minneapolis. Kurt Wagner rebuilt Lambchop around new collaborators, then found his next idea on late-night radio.

years.h: Auto-Tune arrives on This (Is What I Wanted to Tell You)
years.p: Electronic textures and Auto-Tuned vocals from Wagner, another turn for a band once filed under alt-country.

years.h: Trip is all covers
years.p: Lambchop release the album on Merge and City Slang.

years.h: Wagner swaps files with Andrew Broder while caring for his father
years.p: His father battles COVID, a stroke and hip surgery. Wagner trades files with Minneapolis musician Andrew Broder and turns Broder's piano improvisations into songs.

years.h: Showtunes gets made at a distance
years.p: Wagner builds the album remotely with [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]]'s [[James McNew|4182b4da-dc89-4331-bca0-952369bb63fb]], [[Ryan Olson|19bf8c5e-560c-4d85-98fb-51eb5fdc6c5d]] of Gayngs, DJ Twit One and producer Jeremy Ferguson.

years.h: The Bible is recorded in an old Minneapolis paint factory
years.p: Summer 2021 sessions, produced by Andrew Broder and Ryan Olson with a crowd of local players, pull funk, R&B and jazz into Wagner's songs.

years.h: Wagner hears lined-out hymns on the radio, and Punching the Clown follows
years.p: Driving at night, he catches banjo-backed group singing and learns about lined-out hymns, call and response between a leader and a congregation. The new songs go to a small choir.
